- Rendering: no render_gate refusals; every render ran first time.. Judge: The better image wins clearly in all four pairs: B, B, B, A. None of them was close enough to call indistinguishable. The losing frames share one consistent profile. They have competent warm low-sun lighting and pleasant tree-lined shophouse streets. But they are sterile and under-populated, and they repeat assets: the same white van appears in three pairs, silver sedan models are cloned, and the same rain-tree mesh lines every street. Placeholder elements recur too: flat cream or grey block facades, wireframe-looking landmark towers and blob shrubs. Asphalt is uniform and pristine, atmospheric depth is weak, and a heavy HUD with a blank-grid minimap covers the frame. The winning frames each beat this profile on a different axis. Pair 1 wins on crowd density and varied activity, pair 2 on light-and-material interaction and sky drama, pair 3 on surface wear and dynamic composition, and pair 4 on backlit aerial perspective. Only pair 2's B genuinely wowed me. Pair 4's A came close but is marred by blotchy dark specks across the sky. The fixes that would do most for the in-development frames, in order: more pedestrians doing more varied things, more vehicle and prop variety, worn ground surfaces, sharp reflections on cars and glass, and stronger haze and depth for late-day backlighting.
